what: 01225's hir-def half (from no-fallback-front's decision): an impl's elided header lifetimes become fresh early-bound lifetime parameters of the impl, as rustc's resolver fresh_lifetime makes them. Today hir-ty lowers each to '{region error}, so `for<'a> &'a X: Mark` fails through `impl<T: ?Sized> Mark for &T` (hir-ty tests::impossible_items, 01225: rustdoc drops methods whose bounds go through core's impl Copy for &T), and probably hir-ty global_goals' 2 failures (minicore impl Send for &T). Ask: in the impl's GenericParams (the ImplSignature store), add one lifetime param per elided lifetime in the header (trait ref, then self type, in source order), after the explicit lifetimes, with a name no source can write (e.g. '{elided N}). (1) A `&T` with no lifetime and a `'_` in the header lower to LifetimeRef::Param of their param, so hir-ty needs nothing for them. (2) A path segment that gives no lifetime args where its target (resolved in the impl's module scope) has N lifetime params gets N params, and the store records, per such segment, its first implicit LifetimeParamId (a side table hir-ty's path lowering reads; tell me its shape and I do the hir-ty side, path.rs:1566 FIXME, in the same round). Tests: hir-def: GenericParams of `impl<T> Mark for &T` has one lifetime; `impl Tr for Bar<T>` with `struct Bar<'a, T>` has one, recorded for the segment; explicit `impl<'b, T> Mark for &'b T` has only 'b. Tell no-fallback-front-ty-next1 the queue id when it lands.
